audit_method: Repository inspection, full Git history review, read-only aggregate queries against production PostgreSQL (session forced default_transaction_read_only=on, 60s statement timeout). No writes, no DDL, no raw PII retrieved.
project_description: A NestJS + React application giving internal staff filtered, real-time analytics over inbound insurance enquiry ('lead') data held in a PostgreSQL table written by a separate .NET ingestion service. The application is strictly read-only against that shared data and owns only its own authentication/audit tables.

origin_story.predecessor_description: .NET Core service (first commit 2025-09-24; itself a C# reimplementation of an earlier Go API) that ingests inbound leads, validates/normalises UK phone numbers, and forwards them to Noetica (outbound dialer), Marketplace and Leela, plus Brevo contact creation and fleet SMS.
origin_story.problem: The ingestion service sits on the revenue path but had no user interface. Directors and managers had no way to see lead volumes, sources or performance; answering such questions required direct database access.
origin_story.decision: Build reporting as a separate full-stack application reading the same database, rather than extending the ingestion service with reporting endpoints and a UI.
origin_story.reasoning: Reporting is high-churn work (filters, columns, charts, date ranges change constantly). Coupling it to ingestion would mean frequently redeploying revenue-critical infrastructure for analytical reasons. Separation confines reporting failures to 'a chart is wrong' rather than 'leads are lost'.
tradeoffs: No shared validation or domain model
Data access logic duplicated in a second language
origin_story.result: ~8 months and 108 commits of reporting iteration with zero deployments to the ingestion service for reporting reasons.
origin_story.qualification: Rationale reported by the project owner and corroborated by repository structure and the complete absence of any UI in lead-api-dotnet; no written design document predating the decision was found.

dates.note: Dataset predates project by ~13 months; populated by other systems.

integrations: Noetica telephony/dialer (shared database only, no direct API)

architecture.pattern: SPA + REST API + WebSocket, split repositories, cloud-deployed
architecture.auth_model: Google SSO for identity; application database for authorisation. Global SessionAuthGuard verifies JWT then re-reads AuthUser from DB on every request, so revocation is immediate. PermissionsGuard enforces @RequirePermissions.
architecture.session_token_transport: URL fragment after OAuth callback (never sent to servers/logs), stored client-side, sent as Authorization: Bearer. Short-lived httpOnly cookies used only for OAuth state/CSRF.
architecture.realtime: Socket.IO gateway polls SELECT MAX(id), MAX(updated_at) FROM leads every 10s and broadcasts leads:changed; clients invalidate TanStack Query keys. Deliberately not LISTEN/NOTIFY to avoid adding triggers to a non-owned table.

engineering_challenges.title: Re-engineering an inherited client-side data layer (largest technical improvement)
engineering_challenges.inherited_from: Data layer created by gpt-engineer-app[bot] (AI scaffold, Feb 2026), modified by teammate Mati-Sh; client-side XLSX export authored by Mati-Shaikh (Jul 2026)
engineering_challenges.difficulty: fetchAllLeadsForRange ran a sequential while-loop fetching 1,000 rows per request, filtered them client-side by date, accumulated the entire result set in browser memory, and fed six useMemo aggregation passes plus three full-array filter scans. Export consumed the same fully-materialised array. Critically, the loop contained 'if (currentPage > 50) break;' - a 50,000-row ceiling that silently truncated any range beyond ~4 months at the verified rate of ~12,500 leads/month, producing partial dashboard figures presented as complete.
engineering_challenges.solution: Moved aggregation into backend SQL behind GET /internal-leads/dashboard-summary returning computed summary values; moved export to a backend endpoint generating CSV server-side in 2,000-row batches; switched the table to cursor pagination requesting an exact total only on page 1 with a 30s count cache.
engineering_challenges.evidence_level: VERIFIED (architecture and the 50-page cap) / DERIVED (request and row counts)
engineering_challenges.qualification: Request/row counts are arithmetic from the verified code path (1,000 rows per request) and verified production volumes. No wall-clock latency baseline was captured before the change.

engineering_challenges.title: Building on a production database owned by another system
engineering_challenges.difficulty: Any schema change, index, trigger or write risked disrupting a live telephony/dialer system. Standard ORM tooling actively pushes toward migrations and schema reconciliation.
engineering_challenges.solution: Documented read-only posture; local Docker Postgres for all schema work; with-local-db.sh wrapper forcing DATABASE_URL to local for the duration of migration commands; production->local sampling script with read-only enforced at application and Postgres-session level plus hostname guards; auth tables applied to production via reviewed create-only SQL rather than a migration tool.

engineering_challenges.title: Duplicate lead submissions without data loss
engineering_challenges.difficulty: Filtering duplicate=true loses the richer payload; grouping by customer would erase genuine repeat enquiries months apart.
engineering_challenges.solution: SQL gap-and-islands sessionization: normalise mobile/email identity, LAG() to compute gaps, running SUM over >30-minute gaps to form session boundaries, then dual ROW_NUMBER ranking within each session (data richness for the display row, operational completeness for metadata), merged into one canonical row. Same CTE powers list, detail, dashboard and export.

engineering_challenges.title: Cross-origin session auth without cookie complexity
engineering_challenges.difficulty: Frontend and backend on different hostnames; cookie sessions would need SameSite=None, domain alignment and CORS credentials.
engineering_challenges.solution: Session JWT returned via URL fragment (never reaches servers or logs), Bearer header thereafter; httpOnly cookies retained only for the same-origin OAuth state/CSRF handshake. Guard re-reads user from DB every request so revocation is immediate.

engineering_challenges.title: Stale client cache masking correct backend behaviour
engineering_challenges.difficulty: One misconfiguration (PersistQueryClientProvider + refetchOnMount:false) produced three unrelated-looking production bugs: a ~10 req/s reload loop, a count stuck at zero, and a previous user's identity persisting after account switch.
engineering_challenges.solution: Incorporate useIsRestoring() into loading state; re-enable refetchOnMount so stale data self-heals; key the identity query by the token itself so two users cannot share a cache entry.

engineering_challenges.title: Search matching real user behaviour
engineering_challenges.difficulty: Prefix matching failed for partial mobile numbers and for full names pasted from a column that joins two database fields.
engineering_challenges.solution: Substring matching with +44 handling; multi-word searches require each word to match across first_name/surname; 400ms debounce across four tables, deliberately excluding the audit log.

problems_solved.title: OAuth invalid_state on every production sign-in
problems_solved.cause: CSRF state cookie set on *.azurewebsites.net while GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL pointed at the custom domain; two hostnames means the cookie never returns
problems_solved.fix: Pointed frontend production API/WS base at the same custom domain

problems_solved.title: Auth feature deployed but tables absent
problems_solved.cause: No automatic migration step exists by design, to protect the shared leads table
problems_solved.fix: Reviewed create-only SQL applied manually after read-only confirmation the tables did not exist

problems_solved.title: Clean merge silently deleted a colleague's shipped feature
problems_solved.cause: One branch deleted client-side Excel export while another added it; a deletion versus an addition produces no textual conflict
problems_solved.fix: Stopped before pushing, reconstructed both sides, escalated as a product decision rather than choosing unilaterally

lessons: refetchOnMount:false means never refetch on mount, stale or not - not 'skip when fresh'. The library default already implements the intended behaviour.
Investigate duplicates before deleting them; the flagged rows held the richer payload.
'No merge conflicts' is not 'no conflict' - review what a merge did, not its exit code.
Make dangerous operations structurally impossible rather than documented as discouraged.
An error message naming a cause ('session expired') is a hypothesis, not a diagnosis.
Capture baseline metrics before optimising, or the improvement is unprovable afterwards.
